final_proof:
Let \(1\le p<\infty\), and recall that
\[
 \ell ^p=\left\{x=(x_n)_{n\ge1}:x_n\in\mathbb R
       \text{ and }\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|x_n|^p<\infty\right\}.
\]
(If the convention \(p=\infty\) is included, it is addressed at the end.) The stated operations are
\[
 (x+y)_n=x_n+y_n,\qquad (a\cdot x)_n=ax_n\quad(a\in\mathbb R).
\]
Here the second formula is precisely pointwise multiplication in the ambient ring of real sequences after identifying \(a\) with the constant sequence \((a,a,\ldots)\).

First, the operations are closed on \(\ell^p\). For real \(s,t\), convexity of \(u\mapsto u^p\) on \([0,\infty)\), together with the triangle inequality, gives
\[
 |s+t|^p\le (|s|+|t|)^p
 =2^p\left(\frac{|s|+|t|}{2}\right)^p
 \le 2^{p-1}(|s|^p+|t|^p).
\]
Thus, if \(x,y\in\ell^p\), then
\[
 \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|x_n+y_n|^p
 \le 2^{p-1}\left(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|x_n|^p+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|y_n|^p\right)<\infty,
\]
so \(x+y\in\ell^p\). Likewise, for \(a\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|ax_n|^p=|a|^p\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|x_n|^p<\infty,
\]
so \(a\cdot x\in\ell^p\). Hence both operations are well-defined on the asserted sets.

It remains to verify the vector-space axioms. Let \(x,y,z\in\ell^p\), let \(a,b\in\mathbb R\), and let \(n\ge1\). Since equality of sequences is coordinatewise, the corresponding identities in \(\mathbb R\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 ((x+y)+z)_n&=(x_n+y_n)+z_n=x_n+(y_n+z_n)=(x+(y+z))_n,\\
 (x+y)_n&=x_n+y_n=y_n+x_n=(y+x)_n,\\
 (a\cdot(x+y))_n&=a(x_n+y_n)=ax_n+ay_n=(a\cdot x+a\cdot y)_n,\\
 ((a+b)\cdot x)_n&=(a+b)x_n=ax_n+bx_n=(a\cdot x+b\cdot x)_n,\\
 ((ab)\cdot x)_n&=(ab)x_n=a(bx_n)=(a\cdot(b\cdot x))_n,\\
 (1\cdot x)_n&=x_n.
\end{aligned}
\]
The zero sequence \(0=(0,0,\ldots)\) belongs to \(\ell^p\) and satisfies \((x+0)_n=x_n\) for every \(n\). Also \(-x=(-x_n)_{n\ge1}=(-1)\cdot x\) belongs to \(\ell^p\) by scalar closure, and \((x+(-x))_n=0\) for every \(n\). Thus pointwise addition makes \(\ell^p\) an abelian group, and the remaining displayed identities are exactly the compatibility, identity, and two distributive axioms for scalar multiplication. Therefore \((\ell^p,+,\cdot)_{\mathbb R}\) is a real vector space.

If \(\ell^\infty\) is also covered by the notation, the same conclusion holds: for bounded sequences,
\[
 \sup_n|x_n+y_n|\le \sup_n|x_n|+\sup_n|y_n|,\qquad \sup_n|ax_n|=|a|\sup_n|x_n|,
\]
so closure holds, and the coordinatewise verification above is unchanged.
